question.problem:
A small robot makes an error on each task with probability $30%.$ If it performs $4$ tasks, rounded to $3$ decimal places, what is the probability that it makes at most $1$ error?

Rounded to $3$ decimal places, the probability is
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
Let the random variable $X$ be equal to the number of errors the robot makes.

Here, we have the following information:

- There are $n=4$ tasks.

- The probability of an error is $p=30%=0.3.$

So, $X$ follows a binomial distribution, where $X∼B(4,0.3).$

The number of successes of a binomial random variable has the probability mass function

$$
P(X=x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{x}){p}^{x}(1-p)^{n-x},
$$

where $n$ is the number of experiments and $p$ is the probability of success on each experiment.

Substituting the above information into the formula for the probability mass function, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=x) & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{4}{x})(0.3)^{x}(1-0.3)^{4-x} \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{4}{x})(0.3)^{x}(0.7)^{4-x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find the probability that the robot makes at most $1$ error. So, we compute

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 1) & =P(X=0)+P(X=1) \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{4}{0})(0.3)^{0}(0.7)^{4}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{4}{1})(0.3)^{1}(0.7)^{3} \\  & =1(0.7)^{4}+4(0.3)(0.7)^{3} \\  & ≈0.652,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
